chapters.fx: What to watch: CPI 7:30am CT — consensus 3.6% y/y (Reuters 3.7%), 0.6% m/m; core 0.2% m/m, 2.5% y/y is the number the market is actually trading. Bowman 4:40am CT, Barkin 12:30pm, Beige Book 1:00pm CT, Goolsbee 2:00pm CT. Warsh Thu 10:30pm CT; blackout starts Sat Oct 17.
chapters.meaning: What changed: the dollar sat out Asia in full wait mode — DXY 102.16, essentially flat (-0.02%) after Tuesday's -0.35% fade, with every major within hundredths of a percent of the US close. The 10-year parked at 5.221%, the 2-year at 4.782%. Nobody wants a position into 7:30am. The PBoC set the yuan midpoint at 6.7249 — firmer than Tuesday's 6.7298 but weaker than the 6.6922 estimate, i.e. Beijing leaned against yuan strength; a modest signal, no FX shock. FedWatch barely moved: October hike ~23% (hold ~77%), December ~84%. Thread: the hawkish hold is in week six; Tuesday the Fed chorus split in the open — Waller and Williams leaning dovish, Collins and Goolsbee holding the hawkish line — and the dollar gave back the rest of Monday's gain. The thesis has already repriced from 'how many hikes' to 'one and done.' What it means: confirms the stall. The 18-month top is a ceiling while December stays ~84%, and the market has stopped trading the Fed and started waiting on the data. The risk sits in positioning: ~$35.5bn of dollar longs are crowded into a single print.

scenarios.base: DXY holds 101.5-102.5 into the print; the reaction, not the level, is the trade.
scenarios.bear: Soft core (0.2% or below) collapses hike odds; crowded $35.5bn longs squeeze and DXY gives back a percent.
scenarios.bull: Hot core (0.3%+) revives the October hike — DXY breaks out above the 18-month top.

chapters.meaning: What changed: EUR/USD 1.1203 (+0.04%) — flat on the screen, but Lagarde spoke overnight and gave the euro its words for the week: inflation is rising 'predominantly but not exclusively' from energy, there are no second-round effects yet, and the ECB 'cannot wait until they're in full view.' On France, she was blunt: the debt solution 'lies at home in France' — Frankfurt won't underwrite Paris. Lane added that the rise in long-term rates is 'material tightening, relevant for policy stance.' Thread: the euro is stabilizing off the 17-month low on dollar softness plus short-covering — specs are short euros at the ~0th percentile, the most bearish since Feb 2020 — while the French plenary debate grinds on with no verified outcome. Stournaras has December more likely than October for the next ECB move. What it means: confirms the hawkish-hold-but-not-yet stance. 'Cannot wait until in full view' keeps a December hike alive without committing October (~12% priced); the France line puts the fiscal onus on Paris, which is euro-mildly-positive — the spread is a French problem, not an ECB problem.

Thread: the RBA's tightening bias is intact (unanimous minutes, waiting 'could be costly'), and specs are short Aussies at the ~2nd percentile with record gross shorts — the squeeze setup. The $0.70 line is the test. What it means: confirms the policy-vs-sentiment standoff — the China demand signal is real but export-led, not a domestic breakout, so the Aussie still needs the dollar leg to cooperate. A soft US CPI is the squeeze trigger; a hot one kills it.

Spread toward $15 = Hormuz risk back in force; toward $5 = premium truly unwinding. For FX: crude's bounce restores the tailwind for CAD and re-taxes JPY/EUR.
chapters.meaning: What changed: the premium re-bid overnight — Brent +0.7-0.8% to ~$106.4-106.6, WTI +0.6-0.8% to ~$94.7-95.0 and testing $95, after the Saudi energy ministry confirmed a Houthi strike hit an Aramco administrative building in Dhahran (limited fire). Tuesday's settles: Brent ~$105.69, WTI ~$94.14. The coalition struck Houthi fuel sites in Sanaa on Tuesday and UKMTO logged two more Hormuz vessel strikes the same day. OPEC's monthly landed Tuesday: 2026 demand growth cut to 180k bpd (a sixth straight cut, from 380k), 2027 lifted to 2.55M on inventory rebuilding. The Brent-WTI spread sits ~$11.5-11.9 — still wide (normal $3-5): the premium is shipping and geopolitics, not demand. Thread: Monday the market bought the war back; Tuesday it faded the premium on the Russian diesel story; overnight the Aramco confirmation re-bid it. What it means: confirms the 'negotiable premium' read — the market prices a process, with escalation and de-escalation in the same session. Each verified hit re-bids; each diesel headline leaks.
